home_description: Your friendly little toolbox for the web. Format JSON, find what you need, and turn tricky data into a small win. No account needed.
json_intro: Messy JSON? Make it readable, find just the bits you need, or turn it into XML. All in one tidy spot.
privacy_local_text: trick-it is designed for local-first utilities. Files should stay in your browser unless a specific tool clearly discloses that it uploads or sends data elsewhere.
privacy_service_text: The hosting platform may receive ordinary request data such as IP address, user agent, requested path, and timestamps as part of serving the site.
privacy_analytics_text: No analytics requirement is built into the trick-it shell. If analytics are added later, this policy should be updated before collection begins.
privacy_links_text: The catalog links to source repositories. A tool may ask to download declared public assets from the hosts listed in its guide. Those hosts receive ordinary network information such as your IP address, but the platform does not attach your tool input or credentials. Offline files are stored in your browser; clear site data to remove them.
terms_use_text: trick-it provides browser-based utilities on an as-is and as-available basis. You are responsible for checking outputs before relying on them.
terms_files_text: Tools should process files locally in the browser unless a tool clearly states otherwise. Do not submit material you do not have the right to process.
terms_availability_text: Individual tools may change, move, break, or disappear. Open-source software does occasionally develop opinions.
terms_liability_text: To the maximum extent permitted by law, trick-it is provided without warranties and is not liable for losses caused by use of, or inability to use, a tool.
terms_third_text: Registered tools may live in separate repositories and may include third-party open-source dependencies. Their licenses and notices continue to apply.
policy_description: How trick-it validates tools, permissions, offline files, and external assets.
policy_register_text: Tools register through an approved source entry, or optional topic discovery under a trusted owner. Public and private repositories use the same versioned manifest and self-contained HTML bundle contract. The host verifies the repository identity and bundle checksum before publishing.
policy_route_text: trick-it publishes only validated catalog metadata and approved browser bundles. Each tool has a host-owned route and runs in an isolated, opaque-origin iframe. Repository credentials remain in the build environment. Private repositories do not make distributed browser bundles confidential.
policy_behavior_text: New v3 tools declare guides, SEO, permissions and digest-pinned external assets. Legacy v2 tools remain supported without privileged capabilities. Network access inside the iframe remains blocked; the platform verifies approved downloads and mediates supported actions only after consent. Revoke stops future access, not browser permissions or actions already completed. Sandboxing does not prevent excessive CPU use or make tool code confidential. Register reviewed tools only; do not enter secrets into tools you do not trust.
policy_remove_text: A tool may be removed from the registry if it becomes unsafe, misleading, unavailable, or no longer satisfies the manifest contract.
